title: Optional Declaration
explanation: std::optional represents a value that may or may not be present, avoiding sentinel values.

title: Optional Chaining And Transform
description: Chain operations on std::optional with transform and and_then
explanation: C++23 adds monadic operations (and_then, transform, or_else) for clean optional chaining.

title: Variant Declaration
explanation: std::variant holds one value from a set of types, with type-safe access.

title: Variant Visit Pattern
description: Process variant with std::visit using overloaded pattern
explanation: std::visit applies a visitor to the currently held value in a variant.

title: Any Declaration
explanation: std::any stores any copy-constructible type using type erasure.

title: Any Vs Variant Tradeoffs
description: When to use std::any vs std::variant
explanation: Variant is type-safe and efficient for known type sets; any is flexible for dynamic scenarios.

title: String View Declaration
explanation: string_view is a non-owning reference to a character sequence — fast and allocation-free for read-only string operations.

title: String View Operations
explanation: string_view operations like substr, remove_prefix, and remove_suffix are O(1) — no allocations.

title: String View Lifetime Warning
explanation: string_view doesn't own memory — ensure the underlying data outlives the view to avoid dangling references.
